# `security-scope-added`

Required OAuth scope added

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | `wire` |
| **Default severity** | `error` |
| **Rule IDs** | `security-scope-added` |
| **Status** | Implemented (M3) |
| **Group** | Security ([RULES.md section 3](../../RULES.md)) |

## What it detects

An OAuth or OpenID Connect requirement now needs an additional scope.

## Why this default

Tokens issued for the old scopes are rejected.

## Example

From test case [`security-scope-added`](../../test/cases/security-scope-added/): A required scope was added.

`openapi.yaml`, base → revision:

```diff
  …
        - oauth:
          - read
+         - write
        responses:
          '200':
```

Findings:

- `security-scope-added` · error · GET /pets

## Test cases

The example above is the only test case for this rule.


## Policy options

Every rule takes `severity` (`error`, `warn`, `info` or `off`), `fix` and `explanation` in the policy file. The policy file arrives in M6; see [POLICY.md](../../POLICY.md).

```yaml
rules:
  security-scope-added: error
```

## How to fix

Add the new scope as a separate alternative first, or accept tokens with either scope set.
